clue.text: Minor official of the old sultanate

parts.note: ye is an old-fashioned spelling of the
Oman is a sultanate on the Arabian peninsula

explanation.surface: A petty functionary from the days of some Middle Eastern sultan.
explanation.definitionFit: A yeoman can be a minor officer or attendant in a royal or noble household.

clue.text: River with hollowed-out channel I have such power to administer

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon
a cut is a dug channel such as a canal
I have contracts to I've

explanation.surface: A river with a dug channel gives someone the power to run things.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe of I'VE is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: The executive is the arm of government with authority to put laws into effect.

clue.text: Serious about holiday destination …

parts.note: major means serious, as in a major problem
ca, for circa, means about

explanation.surface: Someone is earnest about where to go on holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Majorca is a Spanish Mediterranean island popular with tourists.

clue.text: … and not just the top half of the country

indicators.note: just the top half of keeps only the upper half of the country's name, in a down clue

parts.note: Norway is a Scandinavian country

explanation.surface: Continuing from the previous clue, not only the northern part of the land.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipses link to 3 down's holiday theme. 'just the top half of' keeps NOR of NORWAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Nor is a conjunction meaning and not, as in neither this nor that.

clue.text: Coal fires I dispensed with, moving out of doors

indicators.note: moving tells us the remaining letters shift around into a new order
dispensed with says the letter I is dropped from the words before it

explanation.surface: Someone gets rid of their coal fires and goes to live outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dispensed with' removes I from COAL FIRES, leaving COALFRES; 'moving' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian-derived phrase for in the open air, as when dining outside.

clue.text: Bill swallows fish, with some help

indicators.note: swallows means the first piece takes the second inside it

parts.note: an ad, advertisement, is a bill or poster
the ide is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A man named Bill gulps down a fish with a bit of assistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' poses as a man's name but is a poster; 'swallows' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Aided means helped or assisted, so done with some help.

clue.text: Eccentric American parent's attempt to make dough

parts.note: flaky is slang for eccentric or unreliable
pa is an American word for father, plus the possessive s
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: An odd American father tries to bake.
explanation.definitionFit: Flaky pastry is a type of rich layered dough.

clue.text: Unpredictable crater I observed erupting

indicators.note: erupting says the letters burst out in a new order

explanation.surface: A volcano watcher saw a crater blow its top.
explanation.definitionFit: Erratic means irregular and hard to predict.

clue.text: Produce cracks —- it's a fad

definitions.meaning: to cover with fine cracks, as glaze does

explanation.definitionFit: Craze means to develop a mesh of fine cracks; it also means a short-lived fashion.

clue.text: By most of the panel, journalist is seen as guilty of an offence

parts.note: per means by, as in per post

indicators.note: most of says the last letter is cut from the panel's word

parts.note: a jury is the panel deciding a trial
ED, short for editor, is the crossword's stock journalist

explanation.surface: A jury decides that a reporter has committed a crime.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone perjured has lied under oath, which is the offence of perjury.

clue.text: Overseas using a motorway? By no means

parts.note: ... is a minor British road, by no means a motorway

explanation.surface: Asked whether they drove the motorway when going overseas, someone says not at all.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain roads are graded M (motorway), A and B; a B-road is the humblest of these, so 'a B-road' is 'a motorway? By no means'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being abroad means being in a foreign country, across the sea from home.

clue.text: Six hours during which payments must be made

definitions.meaning: a quarter of a twenty-four-hour day is six hours

definitions.text: during which payments must be made
definitions.meaning: the four days in the year when rents and dues fall due in England

explanation.definitionFit: Taken literally the phrase is a quarter of a day; traditionally it names the four rent-paying dates of the year.

clue.text: Venus never sang it discordantly

indicators.note: discordantly says these letters come out jumbled, as a tune might

explanation.surface: Venus was never sung about out of tune.
explanation.definitionFit: The planet Venus seen in the western sky after sunset is called the evening star.

clue.text: Rather too pretty what we expected, to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Something turned out cloyingly pretty, just as we had predicted.
explanation.definitionFit: Twee describes something excessively quaint, sweet or dainty.

clue.text: Possibly, one's required to enter state

definitions.text: Possibly, one's required to enter state

indicators.note: to enter means one piece goes inside another

parts.note: VA is the postal abbreviation for Virginia, a US state
one's is I'S, one is I, giving IS

explanation.surface: Perhaps you need some document to get into a country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to enter' is the container signal; read as a whole, the clue also describes the document itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A visa is the endorsement often needed before you may enter a foreign country.

clue.text: Watch Tom in Paris, dear -— he's very attractive

parts.note: to eye is to watch
a tom is a male cat
cher is French for dear

explanation.surface: Someone tells their darling to look at a man in Paris because he is gorgeous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tom' is not a man's name here but a male cat.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone striking enough to draw every glance is an eye-catcher.

clue.text: Deer depicted by rising Swiss artist, omitting tail

indicators.note: rising, in a down clue, says the letters are read upwards
omitting tail says the last letter of the artist is dropped

parts.note: Paul Klee was a Swiss-born painter

explanation.surface: A deer painted by an up-and-coming Swiss artist lacks its tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'omitting tail' cuts KLEE to KLE; 'rising' turns that to read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The elk is a large species of deer.

clue.text: Heart-warming, uplifting book, one about a lake

indicators.note: uplifting, in a down clue, says the word for book is read upwards

parts.note: a tome is a large book
I is the Roman numeral one
on means about, concerning
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A moving and inspiring novel about a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uplifting' reverses TOME to EMOT; it also poses as part of the review.
explanation.definitionFit: Something heart-warming stirs the feelings, which makes it emotional.

clue.text: Field well-protected by tower gate

parts.note: a keep is the main tower of a castle
a wicket is a small gate

explanation.surface: A meadow kept safe by a fortified gatehouse.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the wicketkeeper fields behind the stumps wearing pads and gloves, hence well-protected.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep wicket is to field as the padded and gloved cricketer behind the batsman.

clue.text: Old coin, a piece with emperor's head

parts.note: a piece is slang for a gun, a pistol

indicators.note: head picks the first letter of emperor

explanation.surface: An ancient coin shows a profile of an emperor.
explanation.definitionFit: The pistole was an old Spanish gold coin.

clue.text: Reserve an item from the library

definitions.meaning: to reserve a seat or table
a volume borrowed from a library

explanation.definitionFit: To book is to reserve in advance; a book is also the typical library loan.

clue.text: Doctor's son becoming a bishop appears to develop rapidly

indicators.note: becoming says one letter turns into another

parts.note: a surgeon is a kind of doctor
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A doctor's boy enters the church and rises quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'becoming' changes the S of SURGEON into B.
explanation.definitionFit: To burgeon is to flourish or grow fast.

clue.text: Governor has to cry about son

indicators.note: about says the word for cry is turned round

parts.note: to sob is to cry

explanation.surface: A ruler is reduced to weeping over his boy.
explanation.definitionFit: Governor is slang for the person in charge, the boss.

clue.text: Heads off on many active hikes along beach

indicators.note: heads off takes the first letter of each following word

explanation.surface: Ramblers set off on lots of energetic walks along the shore.
explanation.definitionFit: Omaha was a code-named Normandy landing beach on D-Day.

clue.text: Opportunity to make money from strangely varying art

indicators.note: strangely says the letters that follow are arranged oddly

explanation.surface: Weird and changeable art turns out to be a money-spinner.
explanation.definitionFit: A gravy train is an easy source of profit, idiomatically.

clue.text: Something worth having — a way of saving up

indicators.note: up, in a down clue, says the word is read upwards

parts.note: a TESSA was a tax-exempt special savings account in Britain

explanation.surface: Building up savings is a valuable thing to do.
explanation.walkthrough: A TESSA was a 1990s British tax-free savings scheme; 'up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: An asset is a useful or valuable possession.

clue.text: Bizarre king of Egypt finally replaced

indicators.note: replaced says one letter of the king is swapped for another

parts.note: Farouk was the last but one king of Egypt

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of Egypt

explanation.surface: An eccentric Egyptian monarch is at last overthrown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replaced' swaps the final K of FAROUK for T, the last letter of Egypt.
explanation.definitionFit: Far-out is slang for strange or unconventional.

clue.text: Soldier gets near cracking

indicators.note: cracking says the letters break up and reform

explanation.surface: A soldier draws close to breaking down.
explanation.definitionFit: A sergeant is a non-commissioned army rank, so a type of soldier.

clue.text: Government shake-up

indicators.note: up, in a down clue, says the word is read upwards

parts.note: to jar is to jolt or shake

explanation.surface: A reshuffle of the cabinet.
explanation.walkthrough: The Raj was British rule in India.
explanation.definitionFit: Raj is Hindi for rule, used of the British government of India.

clue.text: One employed by the bank beginning to wonder at endless mistakes

indicators.note: beginning to picks the first letter of wonder

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: endless says the final letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: errata are mistakes in print

explanation.surface: A new bank clerk begins to marvel at the errors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the bank' suggests a financial institution, but it is a riverbank, where the water vole lives.
explanation.definitionFit: The water rat or vole makes its home in a river bank: a cryptic use of employed.

clue.text: Catchy tune imposed on Pickwick Club

definitions.meaning: Alfred ... is the swindler who deceives the Pickwickians in Dickens's Pickwick Papers

explanation.definitionFit: A jingle is a catchy tune; it is also the Dickens con man who imposed on Mr Pickwick's club.
